sections.h2: Which offices handle a Daytona Beach home sale?
sections.html:
Daytona Beach sits inside Volusia County, which means the appraiser, tax collector and clerk work at county level. Permits, rental registration and code enforcement belong to the city. Knowing who holds which record spares you a lot of phone calls.

The city is known for its beach, its speedway and its colleges. Your best route depends on the house itself: a tidy home near the water can go on the market, while a rental, an inherited property or a house with heavy repairs often fits a direct as-is purchase.

  • Choose an agent if the house looks good and you can wait for a buyer with a mortgage.
  • Selling it yourself works for owners at ease with contracts and disclosure forms.
  • A cash purchase suits cases where speed, condition or tenants are in the way.

sections.h2: How did Daytona Beach become what it is today?
sections.html:
Daytona Beach was founded in 1870 and incorporated in 1876, and its name is credited to founder Matthias D. Day of Mansfield, Ohio. In 1926 the separate towns of Daytona, Daytona Beach and Seabreeze merged under the Daytona Beach name.

The hard-packed sand made the beach a testing ground for high-speed cars in the early 1900s, and by the 1920s it carried the label of the World's Most Famous Beach. Daytona International Speedway, built by NASCAR founder William France, has hosted the Daytona 500 since 1959. The city notes that driving and parking on the beach is still allowed, which is rare.

Land records give the origin a number: Day bought 2,144.5 acres in the spring of 1871 for $8,000 and paid $1,200 of it up front. The city says its beach draws millions of visitors every year.

Education is part of the picture as well. The city counts six institutions of higher learning within its limits.

sections.h2: Do Daytona Beach landlords have to register their rental?
sections.html:
Yes. In 2024 the City Commission repealed the old Residential License Program and replaced it with a rental registration rule that covers owners of fewer than five units. Registration is annual and applies to long-term rentals, defined as at least six months plus one day.

Rental registration charges, City of Daytona Beach Rental Property Program
ChargeAmount
First-time application$40
First registration, each unit$50
Yearly registration, each unit$75

Owners may ask for a voluntary inspection, and a passing result waives the next year's registration fee. If you want stays shorter than six months plus one day, call the Business Tax Office at (386) 671-8140 to find out whether your zoning permits it. The Rental Property Program office is at 125 S. Palmetto Ave.

Selling a rental? Keep the registration current, because a buyer or title agent may ask to see it, and note that the program covers long-term leases only, so short stays need separate zoning confirmation.

sections.h2: When does Volusia County collect property tax?
sections.html:
Bills leave the Volusia County tax collector's office on or about November 1, and payment is penalty-free through March 31. The collector's page spells out each discount and delinquency step.

  • Pay in November and save 4 percent; December saves 3, January 2 and February 1. March carries no discount.
  • Deferral applications are also due March 31.
  • On April 1 accounts turn delinquent, with a 3 percent minimum charge added.
  • New installment plans must be requested by April 30.

Accounts still unpaid after April 30 are advertised and move toward the annual certificate sale. A certificate sits as a first lien, and two years later it can support a tax deed application, so clear any balance by closing day.

Exemptions run on the state calendar, with the appraiser's deadline on March 1. A homestead exemption can take up to $50,000 off assessed value.

sections.h2: How do permits and code cases affect a Daytona Beach sale?
sections.html:
An unfinished permit or an open code case can appear in a buyer's due diligence. The city's Code Compliance team looks for blighted or substandard housing and presses for its repair or removal.

Look up the permit history on your address before listing. A new roof, an added room or a change to electrical or plumbing without a final sign-off should be resolved first. A cash buyer will take on the house's problems, yet the title company still needs liens and open cases paid or accounted for.

When you request payoff figures, ask the city about unpaid code charges too. Such amounts can follow the parcel and surface in a title search.

sections.h2: What happens when Daytona Beach property taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
After April 30, Volusia County advertises delinquent accounts three times in the newspaper and online. Advertising and auction listing fees are added to the tax notice and cannot be deleted once the notice runs, so paying ahead of the deadline avoids them.

If the bill is still open when the annual certificate sale arrives, the county sells a certificate against the parcel and more charges build up. Redemption requires guaranteed funds, and the collector also takes credit or debit cards for it.

State law lets a certificate holder seek a tax deed two years after April 1 of the issue year. For a homestead, the opening bid includes half of the latest assessed value. If a certificate is outstanding, get the redemption total from the tax collector and budget to pay it out of the proceeds.

Deferral is a separate tool. Homestead owners can file Form DR-570 with the collector by March 31 to postpone the tax above a set portion of household income.

sections.h2: Who collects the deed tax in Volusia County?
sections.html:
The clerk's office takes it at recording. Section 201.02 prices it per $100 of consideration, and the state revenue page lists county rates, where Miami-Dade stands apart.

Every party is liable under state rules, so the contract decides who pays. Recording charges under section 28.24 are billed per page.

Warranty, special warranty, quitclaim and trustee's deeds are all taxable, and a title-moving deed leads to a just-value reset the following New Year's Day.

sections.h2: Which Florida clocks matter if a Daytona Beach seller is in trouble?
sections.html:
Three deadlines come up most often: foreclosure sales, probate and tenant notices.

A foreclosure judgment sets a clerk's sale roughly three to five weeks out, and the top bidder must put down 5 percent. Bid objections have a 10-day limit.

Probate comes first for an inherited house. Summary administration is available when non-exempt assets total $150,000 or less, or when the owner died over two years earlier. Creditors who miss the claim deadline lose their claims.

If a tenant owes rent, the landlord serves a written three-day notice, and following a court order the sheriff gives 24 hours' posted notice. If the house is leased when you sell, put in writing whether the buyer will honor the lease.

faqs.q: Is rental registration required in Daytona Beach?
faqs.a: Yes, for owners of fewer than five residential units under the 2024 ordinance. The yearly fee is $75 per unit after the first year, and passing a voluntary inspection waives the following year's fee.

faqs.q: When do Volusia County taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. A 3 percent minimum charge is added at that point, and accounts unpaid after April 30 are advertised and can go to the certificate sale.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Daytona Beach house with an unregistered rental?
faqs.a: You can, though registering first is wise. Buyers and title agents may want proof the rental complies.

faqs.q: Who collects the deed tax on a Daytona Beach sale?
faqs.a: The county clerk collects it at recording. Section 201.02 sets it per $100 of consideration, and your sale contract says which side pays.

faqs.q: Does selling end my homestead protection?
faqs.a: Yes. The Save Our Homes cap ends at a change of ownership, and the buyer starts at just value the next January 1. Buying another Florida home? The Volusia County Property Appraiser can explain portability.
